Measure total cellular ATP after overexpressing wild-type PFK-X in intact cells.
Measure AMP binding to purified wild-type and R212E PFK-X, then compare activity changes in the same preparations.
Determine whether citrate changes the absorbance of AMP at 260 nm.

questions.explanation: Directly measuring AMP binding and coupling that result to activity would distinguish loss of ligand binding from loss of downstream allosteric communication. If R212E binds AMP normally but is not activated, the mutation likely affects conformational coupling rather than binding. Common miss: Choosing an indirect cellular readout when the mechanistic alternatives concern purified ligand binding and enzyme response. This design directly tests both ligand binding and functional response. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Denaturing SDS-PAGE would assess subunit size, not AMP binding or allosteric signaling.
distractor_rationales.B: Cellular ATP is indirect and would not isolate AMP binding by R212E.
distractor_rationales.D: Citrate effects on AMP absorbance would not test the mutant enzyme's AMP binding or response.

questions.stem: D150N PFK-X is mostly tetrameric but has less than 5% relative Vmax. Which explanation is most consistent with the substitution and the data?

choices.text: D150N increases the Hill coefficient beyond the assay's detection range.
Asp150 is required only for tetramer assembly.
Asp150 is likely important for catalysis or substrate positioning in the active site.
D150N makes AMP a covalent substrate of PFK-X.

questions.explanation: Asp to Asn preserves approximate side-chain size but removes a carboxylate charge. Because D150N remains mostly tetrameric while activity is nearly abolished, Asp150 is most likely important for catalytic chemistry or active-site electrostatics rather than quaternary assembly. Common miss: Equating loss of enzyme activity with loss of oligomerization despite the native gel data. This connects the conservative size change but loss of charge to an active-site functional defect. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: A high Hill coefficient would not by itself explain Vmax below 5%.
distractor_rationales.B: Table p1_t2 shows D150N is 90% tetrameric, arguing against a primary tetramer assembly defect.
distractor_rationales.D: No evidence suggests AMP becomes a covalent substrate.

passages.title: Electron transport, proton coupling, and cytochrome c release
passages.body:
A fictional study examined isolated mitochondria from cultured liver-derived cells. Investigators supplied either pyruvate plus malate, which generate NADH for Complex I, or succinate, which donates electrons through Complex II. They then added inhibitors or a pore-forming BAX-derived peptide. Oxygen consumption, ATP synthesis, inner mitochondrial membrane potential, and cytochrome c detected outside mitochondria were measured. Values are normalized to untreated mitochondria supplied with pyruvate plus malate unless otherwise noted.

Effects of mitochondrial perturbations.
Condition | O2 consumption with pyruvate/malate (%) | O2 consumption with succinate (%) | ATP synthesis (%) | Membrane potential (%) | Cytochrome c outside mitochondria (%)
Control | 100 | 100 | 100 | 100 | 5
Rotenone | 25 | 90 | 35 | 45 | 5
Antimycin A | 10 | 12 | 10 | 20 | 5
Oligomycin | 35 | 38 | 8 | 130 | 5
CCCP | 160 | 155 | 15 | 15 | 5
BAX-derived peptide | 70 | 72 | 60 | 70 | 65

Simplified map of oxidative phosphorylation. — Electrons from NADH enter at Complex I, electrons from succinate enter at Complex II, both pathways pass through ubiquinone to Complex III, cytochrome c, and Complex IV. Complexes I, III, and IV pump protons to create the proton-motive force used by ATP synthase.

questions.stem: Which site of inhibition best explains the rotenone results in Table p2_t1?

choices.text: ATP synthase
Complex II
Complex I
Cytochrome c release pore

questions.explanation: Rotenone strongly lowers oxygen consumption with pyruvate/malate, which supply electrons to Complex I, but succinate largely restores oxygen consumption by entering through Complex II. This pattern localizes the block to Complex I. Common miss: Failing to use the difference between NADH-linked and succinate-linked substrates. This matches the substrate-specific rescue by succinate. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: ATP synthase inhibition would not be bypassed by changing electron entry from Complex I to Complex II.
distractor_rationales.B: A Complex II inhibitor would be expected to impair succinate-supported respiration more strongly.
distractor_rationales.D: Cytochrome c release is not increased with rotenone in the table.

questions.stem: Oligomycin produces a high membrane potential but low ATP synthesis and reduced oxygen consumption. Which explanation best accounts for this pattern?

choices.text: It blocks Complex IV, preventing oxygen from accepting electrons.
It blocks ATP synthase, causing the proton gradient to build and slowing electron transport.
It carries protons across the membrane, eliminating the proton gradient.
It releases cytochrome c from the intermembrane space.

questions.explanation: Oligomycin inhibits ATP synthase. Protons cannot flow efficiently back through ATP synthase, so membrane potential rises; the accumulated gradient makes further proton pumping and electron transport less favorable, lowering oxygen consumption. Common miss: Confusing ATP synthase inhibition with protonophore-mediated uncoupling. This explains high membrane potential, low ATP synthesis, and lower oxygen consumption together. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: A Complex IV inhibitor would lower membrane potential rather than raise it as proton pumping collapses.
distractor_rationales.C: A proton carrier would lower membrane potential and often increase oxygen consumption, resembling CCCP.
distractor_rationales.D: The table shows no increase in cytochrome c outside mitochondria with oligomycin.

questions.stem: CCCP causes high oxygen consumption but low ATP synthesis. Which conclusion is most directly supported by this result?

choices.text: Electron transport and ATP synthesis can be experimentally uncoupled by dissipating the proton-motive force.
ATP synthase directly transfers electrons to oxygen during oxidative phosphorylation.
The proton gradient is unnecessary for mitochondrial ATP synthesis.
Complex II is the only respiratory complex that pumps protons.

questions.explanation: CCCP dissipates membrane potential while oxygen consumption rises and ATP synthesis falls. This supports chemiosmotic coupling: electron transport can proceed, but ATP synthesis requires the proton-motive force. Common miss: Inferring that faster oxygen use must always mean more ATP synthesis. This is directly supported by high respiration with low ATP synthesis and low membrane potential. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.B: ATP synthase does not transfer electrons to oxygen; Complex IV reduces oxygen.
distractor_rationales.C: Low ATP synthesis when membrane potential is low shows the gradient is important.
distractor_rationales.D: Complex II does not pump protons, and the figure states that Complexes I, III, and IV do.

questions.stem: The BAX-derived peptide increases cytochrome c outside mitochondria. In intact cells, this event would most directly promote which downstream process?

choices.text: Replication of mitochondrial DNA by ribosomes
Conversion of pyruvate to lactate in the cytosol
Charging of tRNAs by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases
Assembly of apoptotic signaling complexes that activate caspases

questions.explanation: Cytochrome c release from the intermembrane space is a key signal in intrinsic apoptosis, promoting apoptosome formation and caspase activation. The passage shows BAX peptide specifically increases cytochrome c outside mitochondria. Common miss: Thinking cytochrome c release primarily increases normal electron transport rather than signaling apoptosis. This correctly connects cytochrome c release to intrinsic apoptotic signaling. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Ribosomes do not replicate DNA, and this is not the pathway indicated by BAX-mediated cytochrome c release.
distractor_rationales.B: Lactate formation is a cytosolic redox reaction not directly triggered by cytochrome c release.
distractor_rationales.C: tRNA charging is part of translation and is not the direct consequence of cytochrome c release.

questions.stem: Which conclusion is best supported by the antimycin A data?

choices.text: Blocking Complex III prevents efficient respiration from both Complex I-linked and Complex II-linked electron sources.
Antimycin A selectively blocks only pyruvate import into mitochondria.
Succinate donates electrons downstream of Complex IV.
Antimycin A directly opens the BAX-dependent cytochrome c release pore.

questions.explanation: Antimycin A reduces oxygen consumption to similarly low values with pyruvate/malate and succinate. Because both electron-entry routes converge before Complex III, a Complex III block should impair respiration from either substrate set. Common miss: Treating the succinate condition as an unrelated control rather than a way to map the inhibited complex. This conclusion follows from low oxygen consumption with both NADH-linked and succinate-linked substrates. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.B: If only pyruvate import were blocked, succinate-supported oxygen consumption should remain high.
distractor_rationales.C: Succinate enters through Complex II upstream of ubiquinone and Complex III, not downstream of Complex IV.
distractor_rationales.D: The table shows no increase in cytochrome c outside mitochondria with antimycin A.

passages.title: Regulation of a bacterial nucleotide-reduction operon
passages.body:
A fictional bacterial operon, nrdPQ, encodes proteins required for deoxyribonucleotide synthesis during low-oxygen growth. The operon contains a sigma-factor promoter, a 5' untranslated region with a metabolite M-sensitive attenuator, and a Shine-Dalgarno sequence upstream of the nrdP start codon. When metabolite M binds the nascent 5' untranslated region, a terminator hairpin forms before the coding sequence, reducing production of full-length mRNA. Researchers constructed mutations and measured full-length nrdP mRNA, NrdP protein, and NrdP enzyme activity.

Expression and activity of nrdP constructs.
Construct and condition | Full-length mRNA (%) | NrdP protein (%) | NrdP activity (%)
Wild type, no M | 100 | 100 | 100
Wild type, +M | 30 | 28 | 30
-10 promoter mutant, no M | 12 | 10 | 11
Terminator hairpin disrupted, +M | 95 | 92 | 90
Shine-Dalgarno mutant, no M | 105 | 15 | 14
Active-site Cys to Ser mutant, no M | 100 | 98 | 8

Model of metabolite M-dependent attenuation. — In the presence of metabolite M, the 5' untranslated region folds into a terminator hairpin that causes RNA polymerase to stop before transcribing the nrdP coding sequence. When M is absent or the hairpin is disrupted, RNA polymerase usually produces full-length mRNA.

questions.stem: Which construct in Table p3_t1 most directly identifies a defect in transcription initiation?

choices.text: Terminator hairpin disrupted, +M
Shine-Dalgarno mutant, no M
Active-site Cys to Ser mutant, no M
-10 promoter mutant, no M

questions.explanation: The -10 promoter element is part of the bacterial promoter recognized during transcription initiation. Its mutation lowers full-length mRNA, protein, and activity, consistent with reduced initiation of transcription. Common miss: Equating low protein with transcription failure without checking mRNA abundance. This construct alters a promoter sequence and produces low mRNA, matching a transcription initiation defect. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Disrupting the terminator hairpin increases full-length mRNA in the presence of M, indicating loss of attenuation rather than initiation failure.
distractor_rationales.B: The Shine-Dalgarno mutation leaves mRNA high but protein low, indicating translation initiation impairment.
distractor_rationales.C: The active-site mutation leaves mRNA and protein high but activity low, indicating a catalytic defect.

questions.stem: The Shine-Dalgarno mutant produces nearly normal full-length mRNA but little protein. Which process is most directly impaired?

choices.text: DNA replication initiation
Translation initiation
Polyadenylation of eukaryotic mRNA
Termination of the peptide bond by DNA polymerase

questions.explanation: The Shine-Dalgarno sequence helps position bacterial mRNA on the ribosome for translation initiation. Normal mRNA with low protein indicates the transcript is made but poorly translated. Common miss: Interpreting reduced protein abundance as evidence that the mRNA was not transcribed. This matches the function of the Shine-Dalgarno sequence and the data pattern. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: The construct affects an mRNA translation element, not DNA replication.
distractor_rationales.C: The passage describes a bacterial operon, and polyadenylation is not the relevant process here.
distractor_rationales.D: DNA polymerase does not terminate peptide bonds.

questions.stem: What does the terminator hairpin disruption result most strongly support about metabolite M regulation?

choices.text: M reduces nrdP expression mainly by promoting premature transcription termination.
M prevents ribosomes from forming peptide bonds after full-length mRNA is made.
M changes the genetic code so that UAA encodes tryptophan.
M increases nrdP expression by stabilizing the active-site cysteine.

questions.explanation: In wild-type cells, M lowers full-length mRNA and protein. When the terminator hairpin is disrupted, full-length mRNA and protein remain high even with M, supporting a model in which M represses expression by promoting attenuation before the coding region. Common miss: Focusing on protein output while ignoring that the key restored measurement is full-length mRNA. This is the direct implication of high expression when the M-sensitive terminator cannot form. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.B: If M mainly blocked peptide bond formation after full-length mRNA was made, disrupting a transcription terminator would not restore mRNA and protein so strongly.
distractor_rationales.C: No evidence suggests the genetic code changes.
distractor_rationales.D: M is described as binding the 5' untranslated region, not stabilizing an active-site residue.

questions.stem: The active-site Cys to Ser mutant has normal mRNA and nearly normal protein but very low activity. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.text: The mutation causes metabolite M to form the terminator hairpin even when M is absent.
The mutation prevents RNA polymerase from binding the promoter.
The mutation prevents ribosomes from recognizing the Shine-Dalgarno sequence.
The substituted cysteine is important for NrdP catalysis rather than for transcription or translation.

questions.explanation: Because mRNA and protein abundance remain high, transcription and translation are largely intact. The loss of activity therefore most directly indicates that the cysteine side chain contributes to enzyme catalysis or active-site chemistry. Common miss: Assuming every mutation with low activity must reduce protein expression. This conclusion follows from normal expression but poor catalytic output. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: The data are from no-M conditions and do not indicate metabolite-dependent attenuation.
distractor_rationales.B: A promoter-binding defect would reduce mRNA.
distractor_rationales.C: A Shine-Dalgarno recognition defect would reduce protein despite mRNA production.

questions.stem: Which additional control would best strengthen the conclusion that changes in full-length nrdP mRNA reflect transcriptional regulation rather than unequal RNA recovery between samples?

choices.text: Replace the bacterial promoter with a eukaryotic polyadenylation signal.
Increase metabolite M until all samples have identical enzyme activity.
Measure a stable housekeeping mRNA in each RNA sample and normalize nrdP mRNA to it.
Measure only NrdP protein by Western blot and omit RNA analysis.

questions.explanation: A housekeeping transcript provides a loading and RNA recovery control. Normalizing nrdP mRNA to a stable reference makes it less likely that apparent changes are due to unequal sample input or RNA degradation. Common miss: Choosing another endpoint measurement rather than a control for the measurement being interpreted. This directly controls for RNA recovery and loading across samples. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: A polyadenylation signal does not replace bacterial promoter function and would not address sample recovery.
distractor_rationales.B: Forcing enzyme activities to match would obscure the regulatory effect and would not control RNA recovery.
distractor_rationales.D: Protein measurement alone cannot validate whether mRNA differences reflect transcriptional regulation.

passages.title: Pigment inheritance and enzyme oligomerization in a model yeast
passages.body:
A fictional yeast synthesizes a purple pigment in two steps. Enzyme A converts a colorless precursor to a blue intermediate, and enzyme B converts the blue intermediate to the purple product. Loss of enzyme A prevents blue intermediate formation and produces white colonies regardless of enzyme B genotype. Loss of enzyme B in a strain with functional enzyme A produces blue colonies. The genes A and B are autosomal and are hypothesized to assort independently. Researchers crossed AABB yeast to aabb yeast, then selfed the AaBb F1 progeny.

Observed F2 colony phenotypes from AaBb selfing.
Phenotype | Observed colonies
Purple | 178
Blue | 59
White | 83

Biochemical characterization of enzyme B variants.
Enzyme B protein | Dimeric protein (%) | Km for blue intermediate (mM) | Relative Vmax (%)
B wild type | 95 | 0.10 | 100
b Gly45Asp variant | 25 | 0.12 | 20
b Gly45Asp + stabilizing osmolyte | 70 | 0.11 | 65

Native gel analysis of enzyme B. — Wild-type enzyme B migrates mainly as a dimer. The Gly45Asp variant shows a stronger monomer band and weaker dimer band. Adding a stabilizing osmolyte partially restores the dimer band.

questions.stem: Assuming A and B assort independently, what F2 phenotypic ratio is expected from selfing AaBb progeny in this pathway?

choices.text: 9 purple : 4 blue : 3 white
9 purple : 3 blue : 4 white
1 purple : 2 blue : 1 white
3 purple : 1 white only

questions.explanation: Purple requires at least one functional A allele and one functional B allele (A_B_), giving 9/16. Blue requires A_bb, giving 3/16. White occurs when aa prevents intermediate formation regardless of B genotype, giving 4/16. Common miss: Using a standard 9:3:3:1 ratio without combining the aaB_ and aabb white classes. This correctly applies recessive epistasis of aa over the B locus. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: This swaps the blue and white classes.
distractor_rationales.C: This is a one-gene heterozygote ratio, not a two-gene F2 pathway ratio.
distractor_rationales.D: This ignores the distinct blue phenotype produced by A_bb genotypes.

questions.stem: In the pigment pathway, which genetic interaction best describes the effect of aa on colony color?

choices.text: X-linked inheritance, because both genes are autosomal
Codominance, because A and B are both expressed equally in heterozygotes
Genomic imprinting, because phenotype depends on the parent of origin
Recessive epistasis, because aa masks the phenotypic effect of the B locus

questions.explanation: The passage states that loss of enzyme A produces white colonies regardless of enzyme B genotype. Thus the homozygous recessive aa genotype masks B-locus variation, which is recessive epistasis. Common miss: Calling any two-gene interaction incomplete dominance rather than identifying masking across loci. This correctly describes aa masking the B locus. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: The passage states the genes are autosomal, not X-linked.
distractor_rationales.B: Codominance involves simultaneous expression of different alleles at one locus, not masking across loci.
distractor_rationales.C: No parent-of-origin effect is described.

questions.stem: Which interpretation best explains the biochemical behavior of the b Gly45Asp enzyme B variant?

choices.text: The substitution changes the colorless precursor directly into purple pigment without enzyme A.
The substitution prevents transcription of the B gene, eliminating enzyme B protein.
The substitution greatly increases Km but has no effect on Vmax.
The substitution destabilizes enzyme B dimerization, reducing Vmax while leaving substrate affinity nearly unchanged.

questions.explanation: Table p4_t2 shows low dimer percentage and reduced Vmax for the Gly45Asp variant, with Km nearly unchanged. The osmolyte partially restores dimerization and Vmax, supporting a quaternary-structure stability defect. Common miss: Looking only at the mutation name and not comparing Km, Vmax, and dimerization data. This integrates the native-gel and kinetic data correctly. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: The pathway requires enzyme A to make the blue intermediate before enzyme B acts.
distractor_rationales.B: Purified enzyme B variant is characterized, so the defect is not simply absence of transcription.
distractor_rationales.C: Km changes only from 0.10 to 0.12 mM, whereas Vmax falls strongly.

questions.stem: What phenotypic ratio is expected from crossing Aabb yeast with aaBb yeast?

choices.text: 3 purple : 1 blue only
9 purple : 3 blue : 4 white
1 purple : 1 white only
1 purple : 1 blue : 2 white

questions.explanation: Aabb can produce Ab or ab gametes. aaBb can produce aB or ab gametes. The offspring are AaBb purple, Aabb blue, aaBb white, and aabb white in equal genotypic proportions, giving 1 purple : 1 blue : 2 white. Common miss: Applying the F2 ratio without constructing the gametes for the specified cross. This correctly combines the two white genotypes caused by aa. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: This ignores the white classes caused by aa.
distractor_rationales.B: This is the F2 selfing ratio for AaBb, not this cross.
distractor_rationales.C: This ignores the blue Aabb class.

questions.stem: The F2 cross produced 320 total colonies. If the expected ratio is 9:3:4, which conclusion is most reasonable from Table p4_t1?

choices.text: The data are close to the expected counts for independent assortment with recessive epistasis.
The data prove that A and B are the same gene.
The blue class is absent, so enzyme B is unnecessary.
The observed white count is too low to be compatible with any epistatic model.

questions.explanation: For 320 colonies, a 9:3:4 ratio predicts 180 purple, 60 blue, and 80 white colonies. The observed counts, 178, 59, and 83, are very close to those expectations. Common miss: Judging a ratio by exact equality rather than by reasonable sampling variation around expected counts. This correctly compares observed counts to the expected ratio. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.B: The three phenotypic classes and pathway model do not prove the genes are identical; they support two loci.
distractor_rationales.C: There are 59 blue colonies, and enzyme B is required to convert blue intermediate to purple.
distractor_rationales.D: The white count is close to the expected 80.

passages.title: Pentose phosphate pathway flux during oxidative stress
passages.body:
A fictional erythroid cell line lacks mitochondria after differentiation and relies on glycolysis for ATP. It also uses the oxidative phase of the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) to generate NADPH for reduction of glutathione. Researchers compared wild-type cells with cells expressing a mutant glucose 6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD-M). They exposed cells to an oxidant and measured redox status, lactate release, and radiolabeled carbon dioxide production from glucose labeled at carbon 1 or carbon 6. In the oxidative PPP, carbon 1 of glucose 6-phosphate is released as CO2 while NADPH is produced.

Metabolic responses to oxidant exposure.
Cells and condition | NADPH/NADP+ | GSH/GSSG | Lactate release (%) | 14CO2 from [1-14C]glucose (%) | 14CO2 from [6-14C]glucose (%) | Viable cells (%)
Wild type, basal | 4.0 | 8.0 | 100 | 100 | 5 | 98
Wild type, +oxidant | 2.0 | 4.5 | 120 | 180 | 8 | 92
G6PD-M, basal | 1.5 | 3.0 | 110 | 35 | 5 | 95
G6PD-M, +oxidant | 0.4 | 0.8 | 145 | 40 | 7 | 55

Purified G6PD kinetic parameters.
Enzyme | Km for glucose 6-phosphate (mM) | Relative Vmax (%)
Wild-type G6PD | 0.08 | 100
G6PD-M | 0.09 | 30

Relationship between glycolysis and the oxidative PPP. — Glucose 6-phosphate can enter glycolysis or the oxidative PPP. The oxidative PPP produces NADPH and ribulose 5-phosphate, releasing carbon 1 as CO2. Glycolysis in these differentiated erythroid cells ends mainly in lactate formation.

questions.stem: Why is 14CO2 production from [1-14C]glucose much higher than from [6-14C]glucose in wild-type cells?

choices.text: Glycolysis releases carbon 6 of glucose as CO2 during lactate formation.
The oxidative PPP releases carbon 1 of glucose 6-phosphate as CO2.
ATP synthase oxidizes carbon 1 directly to CO2.
Glucose carbon 6 is converted into the phosphate group of ATP.

questions.explanation: The passage states that the oxidative PPP releases carbon 1 of glucose 6-phosphate as CO2 while producing NADPH. Therefore, [1-14C]glucose is a reporter of oxidative PPP flux in these cells. Common miss: Assuming all glucose oxidation labels behave identically regardless of pathway chemistry. This directly follows from the passage description of the oxidative PPP. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Lactate fermentation does not release CO2 from glucose.
distractor_rationales.C: ATP synthase uses a proton gradient and does not oxidize glucose carbons.
distractor_rationales.D: ATP phosphate groups are not formed from glucose carbon atoms.

questions.stem: Based on Table p5_t2, which kinetic effect best describes the G6PD-M mutation?

choices.text: A large decrease in catalytic capacity with little change in apparent substrate affinity
A large increase in Km with unchanged Vmax
Competitive inhibition by NADPH at the glucose 6-phosphate binding site
Complete absence of glucose 6-phosphate binding

questions.explanation: G6PD-M has a Vmax only 30% of wild type, while Km changes minimally from 0.08 to 0.09 mM. This indicates reduced catalytic capacity or active enzyme performance rather than a major substrate-binding defect. Common miss: Interpreting any loss of pathway flux as an increased Km without checking the kinetic parameters. This correctly compares the Vmax and Km values. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.B: Km changes very little, whereas Vmax changes substantially.
distractor_rationales.C: The table compares purified enzymes and does not show NADPH inhibition.
distractor_rationales.D: If glucose 6-phosphate binding were absent, a meaningful Km near wild type would not be expected.

questions.stem: Which conclusion is best supported by the wild-type response to oxidant exposure in Table p5_t1?

choices.text: Wild-type cells cannot use glucose 6-phosphate in more than one pathway.
Oxidant exposure completely shuts down glycolysis in wild-type cells.
Oxidant exposure causes carbon 6 of glucose to be released preferentially as CO2.
Oxidant exposure increases oxidative PPP flux to support NADPH-dependent redox defense.

questions.explanation: In wild-type cells, oxidant exposure increases 14CO2 from [1-14C]glucose from 100% to 180%, consistent with increased oxidative PPP flux. The NADPH/NADP+ and GSH/GSSG ratios fall but remain higher than in oxidant-treated G6PD-M cells, supporting a redox-defense role. Common miss: Looking only at the decrease in NADPH/NADP+ and missing the increased pathway flux marker. This integrates the label data with NADPH and glutathione measurements. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: The figure shows glucose 6-phosphate can enter either glycolysis or the PPP.
distractor_rationales.B: Lactate release increases to 120%, so glycolysis is not completely shut down.
distractor_rationales.C: 14CO2 from [6-14C]glucose remains low compared with [1-14C]glucose.

questions.stem: The differentiated erythroid cells show very low 14CO2 production from [6-14C]glucose. Which passage detail best explains this result?

choices.text: G6PD directly converts carbon 6 into lactate and CO2.
Carbon 6 is the carbon specifically released by the oxidative PPP.
These cells lack mitochondria after differentiation, limiting complete oxidation of glucose carbons through the TCA cycle.
NADPH is made only by oxidative phosphorylation in these cells.

questions.explanation: The passage states that the cells lack mitochondria after differentiation and that the oxidative PPP releases carbon 1, not carbon 6, as CO2. Without mitochondrial oxidation through the TCA cycle, carbon 6 is not efficiently released as CO2. Common miss: Assuming low carbon-6 CO2 means the radiolabel was not taken up rather than using the pathway map. This correctly uses both the mitochondrial limitation and the carbon specificity of the PPP. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: G6PD acts on glucose 6-phosphate in the oxidative PPP and does not directly convert carbon 6 to lactate and CO2.
distractor_rationales.B: The passage states carbon 1 is released in the oxidative PPP.
distractor_rationales.D: NADPH in the passage is generated by the oxidative PPP, not oxidative phosphorylation.

questions.stem: Which statement best explains the low viability of oxidant-treated G6PD-M cells?

choices.text: Reduced G6PD Vmax limits NADPH production, impairing glutathione reduction during oxidative stress.
G6PD-M cells cannot perform lactate fermentation, so NAD+ is not regenerated.
The mutation increases oxidative phosphorylation until reactive oxygen species disappear.
The oxidative PPP directly synthesizes ATP, so lower G6PD activity eliminates all ATP production.

questions.explanation: G6PD-M has low Vmax and low [1-14C]CO2 production, indicating impaired oxidative PPP flux. Under oxidant stress, these cells have very low NADPH/NADP+ and GSH/GSSG ratios, consistent with inadequate NADPH-dependent glutathione reduction and reduced survival. Common miss: Conflating NADPH production with ATP production and overlooking lactate data. This best connects enzyme kinetics, PPP flux, redox measurements, and viability. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.B: Lactate release is high in G6PD-M cells, indicating glycolytic fermentation continues.
distractor_rationales.C: The passage states these differentiated cells lack mitochondria, and the data do not show increased oxidative phosphorylation.
distractor_rationales.D: The oxidative PPP produces NADPH, not ATP directly; these cells rely on glycolysis for ATP.

passages.title: Kinetic analysis of a cytosolic lactate dehydrogenase variant
passages.body:
Researchers studied LDH-R, a fictional homotetrameric cytosolic lactate dehydrogenase that catalyzes the reversible reaction pyruvate + NADH + H+ -> lactate + NAD+. LDH-R helps maintain cytosolic redox balance when oxidative metabolism is limited. The investigators purified wild-type LDH-R, two point variants, and one truncation variant. Initial velocity was measured at saturating NADH unless NADH affinity was being assessed. PYA is a pyruvate analog that does not undergo reduction.

Properties of LDH-R proteins under selected assay conditions.
Protein or condition | Km for pyruvate (mM) | Relative Vmax (%) | Tetrameric protein (%) | Km for NADH (micromolar)
Wild type, pH 7.4 | 0.10 | 100 | 94 | 25
Wild type + PYA, pH 7.4 | 0.55 | 96 | 93 | 25
H177Q, pH 7.4 | 0.11 | 6 | 92 | 27
L246D, pH 7.4 | 0.12 | 38 | 35 | 26
Wild type, pH 6.6 | 0.08 | 125 | 94 | 22
C-terminal tail deletion, pH 7.4 | 0.28 | 70 | 90 | 80

Initial velocity curves for LDH-R. — At saturating NADH, wild-type LDH-R shows a hyperbolic increase in velocity with increasing pyruvate. PYA shifts the wild-type curve to the right without lowering the plateau. H177Q has a very low plateau. L246D has a lower plateau than wild type. At pH 6.6, the wild-type curve shifts slightly left and reaches a higher plateau.

questions.stem: Which mechanism best describes the effect of PYA on wild-type LDH-R?

choices.text: Competitive inhibition with respect to pyruvate
Uncompetitive inhibition with respect to pyruvate
Irreversible tetramer dissociation
Allosteric activation that increases Vmax

questions.explanation: PYA increases the apparent Km for pyruvate from 0.10 mM to 0.55 mM while leaving Vmax nearly unchanged. Because PYA is a pyruvate analog, this pattern is most consistent with competition at or near the pyruvate-binding site. Common miss: Classifying an active-site analog as allosteric without using the Km and Vmax pattern. This matches increased Km with essentially unchanged Vmax. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.B: Uncompetitive inhibition would lower both apparent Km and Vmax.
distractor_rationales.C: Tetrameric protein remains 93%, arguing against major tetramer dissociation.
distractor_rationales.D: Vmax does not increase in the presence of PYA.

questions.stem: The H177Q variant has nearly normal pyruvate and NADH Km values but very low Vmax. Which interpretation is most directly supported?

choices.text: His177 forms the entire NADH-binding pocket.
His177 is required for LDH-R tetramer assembly.
His177 prevents pyruvate from binding to the active site.
His177 contributes to catalytic chemistry after substrate binding.

questions.explanation: H177Q remains mostly tetrameric and retains near-normal Km values for pyruvate and NADH, but its Vmax falls to 6%. This supports a defect in catalytic turnover, such as acid-base chemistry or transition-state stabilization, rather than a major substrate-binding or assembly defect. Common miss: Assuming that low activity must reflect poor substrate binding rather than impaired catalytic turnover. This best fits preserved binding and assembly with severely impaired catalysis. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: The NADH Km is nearly unchanged, so His177 is unlikely to form the entire NADH-binding pocket.
distractor_rationales.B: Tetrameric protein is 92%, which argues against a tetramer assembly requirement.
distractor_rationales.C: The pyruvate Km is nearly unchanged, so pyruvate binding is not the main defect.

questions.stem: What is the most likely explanation for the reduced Vmax of the L246D variant?

choices.text: The substitution makes NADH unable to bind LDH-R.
The substitution eliminates pyruvate binding at the active site.
The substitution disrupts quaternary structure needed for maximal catalytic output.
The substitution converts LDH-R into an RNA enzyme.

questions.explanation: L246D has a strongly reduced tetrameric fraction and reduced Vmax, while pyruvate and NADH Km values are close to wild type. This supports a quaternary-structure defect that reduces maximal catalytic performance. Common miss: Ignoring oligomeric-state data and attributing every Vmax change to active-site binding. This integrates the low tetramer percentage with reduced Vmax and nearly normal Km values. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: The NADH Km remains close to wild type, so NADH binding is not eliminated.
distractor_rationales.B: The pyruvate Km remains close to wild type, so pyruvate binding is not eliminated.
distractor_rationales.D: An amino acid substitution in a protein cannot convert the protein into a ribozyme.

questions.stem: At saturating NADH and 0.08 mM pyruvate, which condition should give the highest initial velocity among the choices below?

choices.text: C-terminal tail deletion, pH 7.4
Wild type + PYA, pH 7.4
Wild type, pH 6.6

questions.explanation: At a low pyruvate concentration, conditions with lower Km and higher Vmax are favored. Wild type at pH 6.6 has the lowest Km listed and the highest Vmax, so it should have the greatest initial velocity among the options. Common miss: Choosing an enzyme condition by Vmax alone or Km alone rather than considering both at the stated substrate concentration. This condition combines high Vmax with strong apparent affinity for pyruvate. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: The tail deletion has lower Vmax and a higher pyruvate Km than wild type at pH 6.6.
distractor_rationales.B: PYA increases the pyruvate Km substantially, so low pyruvate would poorly support velocity.
distractor_rationales.C: H177Q has only 6% relative Vmax.

questions.stem: Which experiment would best test whether the C-terminal tail deletion directly weakens NADH binding rather than globally unfolding LDH-R?

choices.text: Boil both proteins in SDS and compare only their apparent molecular weights.
Measure lactate concentration in whole cells overexpressing unrelated glycolytic enzymes.
Measure NADH binding to purified wild-type and tail-deleted LDH-R while also assessing folding by circular dichroism or thermal stability.
Sequence the mRNA encoding LDH-R but do not measure protein behavior.

questions.explanation: A direct NADH-binding assay can determine whether the deletion weakens cofactor binding, while an independent folding assay addresses the alternative explanation of global misfolding. The design targets both competing hypotheses. Common miss: Selecting an indirect cellular readout when the competing explanations involve purified protein binding and folding. This directly tests cofactor binding and includes a control for overall protein folding. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Denaturing SDS-PAGE gives subunit size, not native folding or NADH-binding affinity.
distractor_rationales.B: Whole-cell lactate is indirect and confounded by many pathways.
distractor_rationales.D: mRNA sequence does not directly test the biochemical effect of the protein deletion.

passages.title: Alternative splicing and protein dimerization of LUM1
passages.body:
A fictional eukaryotic gene, LUM1, contains four exons. Exon 3 encodes a hydrophobic alpha-helical segment required for stable LUM1 dimer formation. A regulatory RNA-binding protein, RBP-K, binds an intronic splicing enhancer near exon 3 and promotes exon 3 inclusion. Skipping exon 3 preserves the reading frame but produces a mostly monomeric protein that is degraded more rapidly. A separate mutation in the 5' splice donor of intron 2 causes intron retention and introduces a premature termination codon more than 50 nucleotides upstream of the final exon-exon junction.

Effects of LUM1 expression constructs in cultured cells.
Condition | Pre-mRNA transcription rate (%) | Mature mRNA containing exon 3 (%) | Total mature LUM1 mRNA (%) | LUM1 protein (%) | Dimeric LUM1 among detected protein (%)
Wild type | 100 | 85 | 100 | 100 | 80
RBP-K knockdown | 98 | 20 | 55 | 25 | 18
Exon 3 splice acceptor weakened | 95 | 10 | 50 | 20 | 12
Intron 2 splice donor mutant | 100 | 5 | 18 | 6 | 8
Kozak sequence mutant | 100 | 82 | 95 | 22 | 78
Exon 3 hydrophobic-to-charged coding mutant | 100 | 84 | 98 | 45 | 20

Model for LUM1 isoform production. — When exon 3 is included, LUM1 contains a hydrophobic helical segment that supports dimerization. When exon 3 is skipped, the reading frame remains intact but the helical dimerization segment is absent. Intron 2 retention creates a premature stop codon predicted to trigger nonsense-mediated mRNA decay.

questions.stem: Which conclusion is best supported by the RBP-K knockdown data in Table p7_t1?

choices.text: RBP-K directly converts LUM1 protein monomers into DNA.
RBP-K acts as the catalytic subunit of DNA polymerase.
RBP-K promotes exon 3 inclusion without substantially increasing LUM1 transcription initiation.
RBP-K knockdown increases exon 3 inclusion but blocks translation elongation.

questions.explanation: RBP-K knockdown leaves the pre-mRNA transcription rate essentially unchanged but sharply reduces the fraction of mature mRNA containing exon 3. This indicates a role in splicing regulation rather than transcription initiation. Common miss: Interpreting lower protein abundance as evidence of lower transcription without checking pre-mRNA transcription rate. This correctly compares unchanged transcription with reduced exon 3 inclusion. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Proteins are not converted into DNA by RNA-binding proteins.
distractor_rationales.B: The passage describes an RNA-binding splicing regulator, not DNA polymerase.
distractor_rationales.D: Exon 3 inclusion decreases, not increases, after RBP-K knockdown.

questions.stem: The intron 2 splice donor mutant has a normal pre-mRNA transcription rate but greatly reduced total mature mRNA. Which mechanism best explains this pattern?

choices.text: The mutation changes every exon into an intron before transcription begins.
The mutation prevents RNA polymerase from binding the DNA template.
The mutation increases translation initiation at the Kozak sequence.
Intron retention introduces a premature termination codon that promotes mRNA degradation.

questions.explanation: The passage states that the intron 2 donor mutation causes intron retention and creates a premature termination codon predicted to trigger nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. This explains normal transcription but low mature mRNA. Common miss: Assuming low mature mRNA must be caused by low transcription rather than post-transcriptional decay. This directly fits the passage model and the mRNA data. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Exon and intron identity is not globally converted before transcription.
distractor_rationales.B: Pre-mRNA transcription rate remains 100%, so polymerase recruitment is not the main defect.
distractor_rationales.C: Protein is very low, and the mutation is in a splice donor, not the Kozak sequence.

questions.stem: Which process is most directly impaired in the Kozak sequence mutant?

choices.text: Protein dimerization by the exon 3 helix
Spliceosome recognition of exon 3
DNA base pairing during replication
Eukaryotic translation initiation

questions.explanation: The Kozak sequence helps eukaryotic ribosomes identify the start codon. The mutant has nearly normal mature mRNA and exon 3 inclusion but much lower protein, which is consistent with impaired translation initiation. Common miss: Confusing start-codon context effects with mRNA splicing defects. This matches the role of the Kozak sequence and the observed low protein with preserved mRNA. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Among detected protein, dimeric LUM1 remains high, so dimerization is not the primary defect.
distractor_rationales.B: Exon 3 inclusion remains high in the Kozak mutant.
distractor_rationales.C: The mutation affects mRNA translation, not DNA replication.

questions.stem: What best explains the effect of the exon 3 hydrophobic-to-charged coding mutant?

choices.text: It increases the percentage of LUM1 protein that is dimeric.
It prevents exon 3 from being transcribed into pre-mRNA.
It causes the spliceosome to remove all mature mRNA caps.
It disrupts the protein-protein interface required for LUM1 dimerization.

questions.explanation: The coding mutant leaves transcription, exon 3 inclusion, and total mature mRNA nearly normal but greatly reduces dimeric LUM1. Replacing hydrophobic residues in a dimerization helix with charged residues is likely to disrupt the protein interface. Common miss: Attributing a coding-region protein-structure defect to altered splicing despite normal exon inclusion. This directly connects the coding change to reduced dimer formation. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Dimeric LUM1 decreases from 80% to 20%.
distractor_rationales.B: Pre-mRNA transcription and exon 3-containing mRNA remain high.
distractor_rationales.C: The spliceosome does not remove mature mRNA caps, and the data do not support cap loss.

questions.stem: Which experiment would best test whether the low mature mRNA in the intron 2 splice donor mutant is caused by nonsense-mediated decay?

choices.text: Replace exon 3 with a mitochondrial electron transport protein and measure oxygen consumption only.
Increase the amount of charged tRNA in the culture medium and measure DNA replication.
Reduce a core nonsense-mediated decay factor and measure whether the intron-retaining LUM1 transcript accumulates.
Boil the cells before RNA extraction to improve splice-site recognition.

questions.explanation: If nonsense-mediated decay is degrading the mutant transcript, reducing an essential decay factor should increase the abundance of the intron-retaining mRNA. Measuring the specific transcript tests the proposed mechanism directly. Common miss: Testing protein output instead of directly testing the RNA decay mechanism proposed by the passage. This experiment directly perturbs the proposed decay pathway and measures the relevant RNA species. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Oxygen consumption would not isolate nonsense-mediated decay of LUM1 mRNA.
distractor_rationales.B: Charged tRNAs do not directly test mRNA decay of a premature-stop transcript.
distractor_rationales.D: Boiling cells would damage biomolecules and would not improve splice-site recognition.

passages.title: Fidelity of a threonyl-tRNA synthetase
passages.body:
A fictional threonyl-tRNA synthetase, ThrRS-F, attaches threonine to tRNAThr during translation. The first active site activates threonine by forming threonyl-AMP from threonine and ATP; the amino acid is then transferred to the 3' end of tRNAThr. Because valine is structurally similar to threonine, ThrRS-F also contains an editing domain that hydrolyzes mischarged Val-tRNAThr. A reporter protein loses activity when valine is inserted at positions normally encoded by threonine codons.

Aminoacylation and editing properties of ThrRS-F.
Condition | Thr-tRNAThr charging rate (%) | Val-tRNAThr accumulation (%) | ATP-to-AMP conversion rate (%) | Active reporter protein (%)
Wild-type ThrRS-F + wild-type tRNAThr | 100 | 1 | 100 | 98
Editing-site D201A + wild-type tRNAThr | 95 | 28 | 125 | 62
Activation-site K55A + wild-type tRNAThr | 8 | 1 | 10 | 12
Wild-type ThrRS-F + acceptor-stem mutant tRNAThr | 18 | 1 | 22 | 20
Editing-site D201A + excess free valine | 90 | 45 | 140 | 45
Wild-type ThrRS-F + noncognate tRNAAla | 3 | 0.5 | 5 | 8

Two-site model of ThrRS-F specificity. — The activation site forms aminoacyl-AMP intermediates using ATP. Correct threonylated tRNA is released for translation. Incorrect Val-tRNAThr can enter an editing domain, where the aminoacyl ester bond is hydrolyzed before the tRNA reaches the ribosome.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which reaction most directly accounts for ATP-to-AMP conversion by ThrRS-F?

choices.text: Peptide bond formation between two amino acids
Formation of an aminoacyl-AMP intermediate
Hydrolysis of the phosphodiester backbone of tRNA
Oxidation of NADH by Complex I

questions.explanation: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases activate amino acids by using ATP to form aminoacyl-AMP intermediates. The passage states that ThrRS-F forms threonyl-AMP from threonine and ATP. Common miss: Attributing ATP use in tRNA charging to the ribosome rather than the aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase. This is the ATP-dependent activation step described in the passage. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Peptide bond formation occurs on the ribosome and does not explain ATP-to-AMP conversion by ThrRS-F.
distractor_rationales.C: tRNA backbone hydrolysis is not part of normal aminoacylation.
distractor_rationales.D: Complex I is part of oxidative phosphorylation and is unrelated to ThrRS-F amino acid activation.

questions.stem: Which interpretation best explains the phenotype of the editing-site D201A variant?

choices.text: The variant cannot recognize any tRNA molecule.
Threonine cannot be activated, so ATP-to-AMP conversion is nearly absent.
Amino acid activation is mostly intact, but hydrolysis of mischarged Val-tRNAThr is impaired.
The variant improves reporter activity by eliminating translation errors.

questions.explanation: D201A maintains high Thr-tRNAThr charging and high ATP-to-AMP conversion but accumulates much more Val-tRNAThr and lowers reporter activity. This indicates a specific editing defect rather than failure of activation or tRNA recognition. Common miss: Treating editing failure as the same as failure to aminoacylate the tRNA. This matches high charging with increased mischarged tRNA accumulation. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: The enzyme still charges wild-type tRNAThr efficiently.
distractor_rationales.B: Charging and ATP-to-AMP conversion remain high, so activation is not nearly absent.
distractor_rationales.D: Reporter activity decreases, consistent with more translation errors.

questions.stem: What is the most likely direct effect of the activation-site K55A substitution?

choices.text: Reduced formation of aminoacyl-AMP intermediates
Enhanced hydrolysis of correctly charged Thr-tRNAThr
Increased recognition of tRNAAla as tRNAThr
Creation of a new stop codon in the reporter mRNA

questions.explanation: K55A has low Thr-tRNAThr charging and low ATP-to-AMP conversion. Because K55 is in the activation site, the best interpretation is that amino acid activation through aminoacyl-AMP formation is impaired. Common miss: Attributing low charging to editing rather than to the ATP-dependent activation step. This directly explains reduced ATP-to-AMP conversion and poor charging. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.B: The data do not show excessive hydrolysis of correctly charged tRNA.
distractor_rationales.C: The condition with noncognate tRNAAla is not the K55A condition, and no enhanced recognition is shown.
distractor_rationales.D: The enzyme substitution does not alter the reporter mRNA codons.

questions.stem: The acceptor-stem mutant tRNAThr produces low charging even with wild-type ThrRS-F. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.text: The acceptor stem is the site where ribosomes synthesize DNA.
The acceptor stem contains identity elements important for recognition by ThrRS-F.
The acceptor-stem mutation increases editing of valine to threonine.
ThrRS-F no longer requires ATP when the acceptor stem is changed.

questions.explanation: Wild-type ThrRS-F charges acceptor-stem mutant tRNAThr poorly, indicating that tRNA structural features in the acceptor stem contribute to proper recognition and aminoacylation. Common miss: Viewing tRNAs as interchangeable adapters rather than molecules with recognition determinants. This directly follows from poor charging of the altered tRNA. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Ribosomes synthesize proteins, not DNA.
distractor_rationales.C: Editing hydrolyzes mischarged tRNA; it does not convert valine into threonine.
distractor_rationales.D: ATP-to-AMP conversion is reduced, not made unnecessary.

questions.stem: Which experiment would best test whether the reduced reporter activity in the D201A condition is caused by valine misincorporation at threonine-coded positions?

choices.text: Analyze reporter peptides by mass spectrometry to detect valine at positions normally occupied by threonine.
Measure only total ATP concentration in the culture medium.
Delete all threonine codons from the genetic code.
Assay Complex IV activity in isolated mitochondria.

questions.explanation: Mass spectrometry of reporter peptides can directly identify amino acids incorporated at specific positions. Detecting valine at positions encoded by threonine codons would support the proposed translation-fidelity mechanism. Common miss: Using an indirect activity readout when the hypothesis concerns specific amino acid misincorporation. This directly tests the predicted molecular error in the reporter protein. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.B: Total ATP concentration would not reveal which amino acids were incorporated.
distractor_rationales.C: Codons cannot be deleted from the genetic code in this experimental context.
distractor_rationales.D: Complex IV activity is unrelated to reporter mistranslation by ThrRS-F.

passages.title: Nuclear genes required for Complex IV assembly in a model alga
passages.body:
A fictional unicellular alga uses nuclear genes E and F to assemble functional mitochondrial Complex IV. Gene E encodes a copper-delivery chaperone, and gene F encodes a Complex IV structural subunit. Loss of either gene produces a slow-respiration phenotype, and loss of both genes is not more severe than loss of either single gene. The genes are autosomal and assort independently. Researchers crossed EEFF algae with eeff algae, selfed the EeFf F1, and measured F2 respiration phenotypes. Biochemical assays were performed on representative genotypes.

F2 respiration phenotypes after EeFf selfing.
Phenotype | Observed colonies
Normal respiration | 166
Slow respiration | 126

Respiratory measurements in representative strains.
Strain or condition | Complex I activity (%) | Complex IV activity (%) | O2 consumption (%) | NADH/NAD+ ratio | Growth on fermentable carbon
E_F_ | 100 | 100 | 100 | 0.5 | Robust
eeF_ | 95 | 18 | 22 | 3.2 | Slow but viable
E_ff | 100 | 20 | 25 | 3.0 | Slow but viable
eeff | 93 | 15 | 20 | 3.4 | Slow but viable
E_F_ + Complex IV inhibitor | 98 | 5 | 8 | 4.0 | Poor

Electron flow to Complex IV. — Electrons from NADH enter through Complex I and are transferred through ubiquinone, Complex III, cytochrome c, and Complex IV. Complex IV transfers electrons to oxygen. When Complex IV activity is low, upstream electron carriers become more reduced and oxygen consumption falls.

questions.stem: If genes E and F assort independently and both are required for normal respiration, what F2 phenotypic ratio is expected after selfing EeFf algae?

choices.text: 1 normal : 1 slow
9 normal : 3 slow : 4 lethal
3 normal : 1 slow
9 normal : 7 slow

questions.explanation: Normal respiration requires at least one functional E allele and one functional F allele, giving E_F_ = 9/16. All other genotypes lack at least one required component and are slow, giving 7/16. Common miss: Using a standard 9:3:3:1 ratio without combining all genotypes missing either required gene. This correctly applies complementary gene action for two independently assorting genes. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: This is a simple testcross-like ratio, not the expected F2 ratio from EeFf selfing.
distractor_rationales.B: No lethal class is described, and loss of both genes is not more severe than single loss.
distractor_rationales.C: This is a one-gene heterozygote self-cross ratio.

questions.stem: Which conclusion is best supported by the representative strain data in Table p9_t2?

choices.text: Genes E and F are both required for normal Complex IV activity.
Gene E is required for Complex I activity, whereas gene F is not.
The double mutant has much higher respiration than either single mutant.
Loss of either gene increases oxygen consumption by accelerating Complex IV.

questions.explanation: Both eeF_ and E_ff strains have normal Complex I activity but low Complex IV activity and low oxygen consumption. The double mutant is similar, supporting the conclusion that E and F are both needed for normal Complex IV function. Common miss: Assuming that any respiratory defect must originate at Complex I rather than using the measured complex activities. This matches the low Complex IV activity when either gene is lost. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.B: Complex I activity remains near normal in all mutant strains.
distractor_rationales.C: The double mutant has low respiration similar to the single mutants.
distractor_rationales.D: Oxygen consumption decreases when either gene is lost.

questions.stem: Why is the NADH/NAD+ ratio elevated in strains with low Complex IV activity?

choices.text: Complex IV inhibition increases the amount of oxygen available as a carbon source.
Complex IV directly synthesizes NADH from ATP and oxygen.
Blocked downstream electron transfer slows NADH oxidation, causing upstream carriers to remain more reduced.
Loss of Complex IV forces NADH to become a peptide bond donor.

questions.explanation: Complex IV transfers electrons to oxygen. When Complex IV is deficient, electrons accumulate upstream and NADH oxidation slows, increasing the NADH/NAD+ ratio. Common miss: Predicting that low oxygen consumption means NADH must be depleted rather than accumulated. This correctly links downstream blockade to reduced upstream carriers. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor, not a carbon source in this context.
distractor_rationales.B: Complex IV does not synthesize NADH from ATP.
distractor_rationales.D: NADH does not donate peptide bonds.

questions.stem: A slow-respiration eeFF strain is crossed with a slow-respiration EEff strain. What phenotype is expected for the diploid EeFf progeny if the mutations affect different genes as described?

choices.text: No growth on fermentable carbon
Slow respiration identical to eeff
Normal respiration
Respiration faster than wild type because both mutations complement excessively

questions.explanation: The cross restores one functional allele at each gene, producing EeFf progeny. Because both E and F functions are present, normal respiration is expected under the complementary gene model. Common miss: Confusing complementation between different genes with failure to complement alleles of the same gene. This correctly predicts complementation between mutations in different genes. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: The passage states even mutant strains are slow but viable on fermentable carbon.
distractor_rationales.B: EeFf contains functional alleles of both genes and should not resemble eeff.
distractor_rationales.D: Complementation restores normal function but does not imply respiration above wild type.

questions.stem: Which additional measurement would best help determine whether the low Complex IV activity in mutants reflects a specific Complex IV assembly defect rather than fewer mitochondria per cell?

choices.text: Normalize Complex IV activity to a mitochondrial marker such as citrate synthase activity or mitochondrial protein content.
Measure colony color under a microscope without assaying respiration.
Remove oxygen from all cultures before measuring Complex IV activity.
Measure only cytosolic ribosome abundance.

questions.explanation: A mitochondrial marker provides a control for mitochondrial abundance. If Complex IV activity remains selectively low after normalization, the result supports a specific assembly or Complex IV functional defect. Common miss: Accepting a lower enzyme activity measurement without considering whether there is less organelle material in the sample. This directly addresses the alternative explanation of reduced mitochondrial mass. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.B: Colony color is not a direct control for mitochondrial abundance or Complex IV activity.
distractor_rationales.C: Removing oxygen would interfere with respiratory measurement rather than control for mitochondrial content.
distractor_rationales.D: Cytosolic ribosome abundance does not indicate mitochondrial abundance.

passages.title: Gluconeogenic flux in hepatocyte-like cells
passages.body:
Researchers used fictional hepatocyte-like HGL cells to study glucose production from lactate and alanine. Pyruvate generated in the cytosol must enter mitochondria through the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (MPC). In the mitochondrial matrix, pyruvate carboxylase (PC) uses ATP, bicarbonate, and a biotin cofactor to convert pyruvate to oxaloacetate. Phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase (PEPCK) then uses GTP to convert oxaloacetate to phosphoenolpyruvate. The pathway requires substantial energy input and is sensitive to cellular ATP availability.

Metabolic effects of perturbing gluconeogenesis from lactate and alanine.
Condition | Glucose output (%) | Cytosolic pyruvate (%) | Mitochondrial OAA/malate pool (%) | O2 consumption (%) | ATP/ADP ratio
Control | 100 | 100 | 100 | 100 | 5.0
MPC inhibitor B | 20 | 190 | 35 | 90 | 4.8
PC inhibitor C | 12 | 220 | 28 | 82 | 3.9
PEPCK knockdown | 18 | 120 | 210 | 85 | 4.2
Low-dose ETC inhibitor | 44 | 115 | 82 | 34 | 1.5
Acetyl-CoA analog | 135 | 70 | 155 | 112 | 4.6

Simplified route from lactate and alanine to glucose. — Lactate and alanine are converted to cytosolic pyruvate. Pyruvate enters mitochondria through MPC and is carboxylated by PC to oxaloacetate. Oxaloacetate-derived carbon returns to the cytosol and proceeds through gluconeogenic reactions to form glucose.

questions.stem: Which interpretation best explains the effect of PC inhibitor C in Table p10_t1?

choices.text: MPC import is accelerated, preventing cytosolic pyruvate accumulation.
PEPCK activity is increased, causing oxaloacetate to accumulate.
Pyruvate enters or accumulates, but conversion to mitochondrial oxaloacetate is impaired.
Gluconeogenesis increases because PC normally inhibits glucose output.

questions.explanation: PC inhibitor C causes high cytosolic pyruvate, low mitochondrial OAA/malate pool, and very low glucose output. This supports a block at pyruvate carboxylase, which normally converts mitochondrial pyruvate to oxaloacetate. Common miss: Interpreting pyruvate accumulation as evidence of increased pathway flux rather than a downstream block. This matches the accumulation of pyruvate with depletion of downstream OAA/malate. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Cytosolic pyruvate increases, not decreases, with PC inhibitor C.
distractor_rationales.B: PEPCK knockdown, not PC inhibition, causes OAA/malate accumulation in the table.
distractor_rationales.D: Glucose output falls, showing PC supports rather than inhibits gluconeogenesis in this context.

questions.stem: Which finding most strongly distinguishes PEPCK knockdown from PC inhibition?

choices.text: PEPCK knockdown eliminates cytosolic pyruvate, whereas PC inhibition has no effect on pyruvate.
PEPCK knockdown increases glucose output, whereas PC inhibition lowers glucose output.
PEPCK knockdown causes accumulation of the mitochondrial OAA/malate pool, whereas PC inhibition lowers it.
PEPCK knockdown raises ATP/ADP to a higher value than control.

questions.explanation: PC acts before oxaloacetate formation, so PC inhibition lowers the OAA/malate pool. PEPCK acts after oxaloacetate formation, so PEPCK knockdown causes OAA/malate accumulation while still lowering glucose output. Common miss: Using glucose output alone, even though multiple different blocks can reduce glucose output. This correctly uses the opposite OAA/malate pool changes to localize the blocks. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Both conditions show elevated cytosolic pyruvate relative to control.
distractor_rationales.B: Both perturbations lower glucose output.
distractor_rationales.D: ATP/ADP is lower than control with PEPCK knockdown.

questions.stem: Why does the low-dose ETC inhibitor reduce glucose output in HGL cells?

choices.text: The ETC inhibitor directly removes all lactate and alanine from the medium.
Reduced oxidative phosphorylation lowers ATP availability for energy-requiring gluconeogenic steps.
The ETC inhibitor converts glucose into mitochondrial DNA.
Reduced O2 consumption necessarily means PC becomes more active than control.

questions.explanation: The passage states that gluconeogenesis requires substantial energy input. The ETC inhibitor lowers O2 consumption and ATP/ADP ratio, so reduced ATP availability provides a plausible explanation for lower glucose output. Common miss: Treating gluconeogenesis as energy-neutral and ignoring the ATP/ADP measurement. This integrates the lower O2 consumption, lower ATP/ADP ratio, and energy requirement of gluconeogenesis. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: No passage data indicate removal of lactate or alanine from the medium.
distractor_rationales.C: Glucose is not converted into mitochondrial DNA.
distractor_rationales.D: The ETC inhibitor lowers the OAA/malate pool and glucose output; increased PC activity is not supported.

questions.stem: The acetyl-CoA analog increases glucose output and the mitochondrial OAA/malate pool. Which mechanism is most consistent with this observation?

choices.text: Allosteric activation of pyruvate carboxylase increases conversion of pyruvate to oxaloacetate.
Direct inhibition of MPC prevents pyruvate from reaching mitochondria.
Destruction of ATP prevents gluconeogenesis from consuming energy.
Conversion of oxaloacetate into ribosomal RNA increases translation.

questions.explanation: The acetyl-CoA analog lowers cytosolic pyruvate, raises the mitochondrial OAA/malate pool, and increases glucose output. This pattern fits activation of PC, which converts pyruvate to oxaloacetate. Common miss: Calling any metabolite analog an inhibitor without using the measured direction of pathway flux. This correctly explains the direction of pyruvate, OAA/malate, and glucose-output changes. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.B: MPC inhibition produces the opposite pattern of high cytosolic pyruvate and low OAA/malate.
distractor_rationales.C: The ATP/ADP ratio remains high enough and glucose output rises, not falls.
distractor_rationales.D: Oxaloacetate is a metabolic intermediate, not a direct precursor to ribosomal RNA in the described pathway.

questions.stem: Which experiment would best distinguish whether inhibitor B primarily blocks mitochondrial pyruvate import rather than directly inhibiting PC catalysis?

choices.text: Measure radiolabeled pyruvate uptake into isolated mitochondria and separately assay PC activity in disrupted mitochondrial extracts supplied with pyruvate.
Measure only total glucose output in intact cells after adding inhibitor B.
Sequence ribosomal RNA to determine whether pyruvate codons changed.
Add a Complex IV inhibitor and assume any further decrease identifies the MPC target.

questions.explanation: Directly measuring mitochondrial pyruvate uptake tests the transport hypothesis, while measuring PC activity in disrupted extracts bypasses membrane import and tests whether PC catalysis itself is inhibited. Together, these assays distinguish transporter inhibition from enzyme inhibition. Common miss: Using a whole-pathway endpoint when the mechanistic alternatives require separate transport and enzyme assays. This design separately tests pyruvate import and PC catalytic activity. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.B: Total glucose output alone cannot localize the inhibited step.
distractor_rationales.C: Ribosomal RNA sequence is unrelated to pyruvate import or PC catalysis.
distractor_rationales.D: Adding an ETC inhibitor would introduce an energy confound and would not identify the primary target of inhibitor B.

passages.title: Study of Notification Cues and Attention
passages.body:
Researchers investigated how smartphone notification cues affect attention and perceived stress. Eighty undergraduate volunteers completed a computerized reaction-time task in three counterbalanced conditions: no notification, a vibration notification, and a visual banner notification. In each condition, participants pressed a key as soon as a target shape appeared. The phone was placed face down for the vibration condition and face up for the visual banner condition. Participants were told that notifications were unrelated to task performance and did not require a response. After each condition, participants rated their momentary stress on a 1 to 7 scale. The researchers also measured whether participants reported checking their phones within 30 seconds after the task.

Mean task performance and stress ratings by notification condition
Condition | Mean reaction time to target (ms) | Error rate (%) | Mean stress rating
No notification | 420 | 4 | 2.1
Vibration notification | 470 | 6 | 3.4
Visual banner notification | 445 | 5 | 2.8

Phone-checking behavior after task
Condition | Percent checking phone within 30 seconds
No notification | 12
Vibration notification | 48
Visual banner notification | 31

Design summary — Each participant completed all three notification conditions in randomized order. The primary dependent variables were reaction time, error rate, stress rating, and post-task phone checking.

questions.stem: Which conclusion is best supported by the reaction-time data in Table 1?

choices.text: Vibration notifications improved target detection by increasing arousal.
Visual banner notifications eliminated attentional distraction.
Notification condition had no relationship to performance because all error rates were below 10%.
Vibration notifications were associated with slower responses than the no-notification condition.

questions.explanation: The mean reaction time was 420 ms with no notification and 470 ms with vibration notification. This supports the conclusion that vibration notifications were associated with slower responses in this task. The data do not show elimination of distraction or improved detection. Common miss: Ignoring reaction-time differences because the error rates appear numerically small. This is correct. The vibration condition had the slowest mean reaction time. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: The vibration condition was associated with slower responses and higher errors, not improved detection.
distractor_rationales.B: The visual banner condition still had a slower mean reaction time and higher error rate than no notification, so distraction was not eliminated.
distractor_rationales.C: Low error rates do not imply no performance relationship; reaction time varied across conditions.

questions.stem: The vibration notification most likely increased phone checking because the vibration had previously been paired with incoming messages in participants' daily lives. In learning terms, the vibration would best be described as a:

choices.text: Punisher
Unconditioned stimulus
Negative reinforcer
Conditioned stimulus

questions.explanation: A phone vibration can become a conditioned stimulus if it is repeatedly paired with meaningful notifications. It can then evoke orienting, checking, or arousal even when the current message does not require a response. Common miss: Confusing a cue that predicts an event with a reinforcer that follows and strengthens a behavior. This is correct. A formerly neutral vibration can acquire meaning through repeated association with messages. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: A punisher decreases behavior when applied or removed; the observed checking behavior increased after notifications.
distractor_rationales.B: An unconditioned stimulus naturally elicits a response without prior learning; a phone vibration does not inherently signal social information.
distractor_rationales.C: A negative reinforcer increases behavior by removing an aversive stimulus, which is not what the vibration itself represents.

questions.stem: Which feature of the study design most directly helps reduce individual-difference confounding across notification conditions?

choices.text: The phone was face down during the vibration condition.
Each participant completed all three notification conditions.
Participants rated stress after each condition.
Participants were told notifications did not require a response.

questions.explanation: A within-subject design means each participant serves as their own comparison across conditions. This reduces confounding from stable individual differences, such as baseline reaction speed or general phone attachment. Common miss: Selecting a measurement procedure rather than the design feature that makes participants comparable across conditions. This is correct. Repeated measurement across all conditions controls many person-level differences. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Phone orientation defines part of the manipulation but does not control individual differences across conditions as directly.
distractor_rationales.C: Stress ratings provide a dependent variable; they do not by themselves reduce confounding.
distractor_rationales.D: This instruction standardizes expectations but does not control individual differences as strongly as the within-subject design.

questions.stem: Which additional result would most strengthen the interpretation that notifications disrupted selective attention rather than only increasing motor slowing?

choices.text: Participants reported owning phones for similar numbers of years.
Participants had the same resting heart rate before each condition.
Participants showed greater slowing on trials in which distracting shapes appeared near the target.
Participants completed the visual banner condition before the vibration condition.

questions.explanation: Selective attention involves prioritizing task-relevant stimuli while filtering distractors. A disproportionate slowing when distracting shapes are present would support an attentional filtering explanation rather than a general motor slowing explanation. Common miss: Choosing a general control variable instead of a result that distinguishes between two competing mechanisms. This is correct. It links the notification effect specifically to distractor processing and attentional control. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Similar phone ownership duration would not directly test the mechanism of slower task responses.
distractor_rationales.B: Equivalent resting heart rate would address baseline physiology but not distinguish attentional disruption from motor slowing.
distractor_rationales.D: A fixed order could introduce order effects and would not clarify the attentional mechanism.

questions.stem: Based on Table 2, what is the approximate percentage-point increase in phone checking from the no-notification condition to the vibration condition?

choices.text: 19 percentage points
31 percentage points
36 percentage points
48 percentage points

questions.explanation: Phone checking occurred in 12% of the no-notification condition and 48% of the vibration condition. The increase is 48 minus 12, or 36 percentage points. Common miss: Reporting the final percentage rather than the percentage-point difference between conditions. This is correct. The difference is 48% minus 12% = 36 percentage points. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: This subtracts 12 from 31, comparing visual banner to no notification rather than vibration to no notification.
distractor_rationales.B: This is the visual banner percentage, not the increase from no notification to vibration.
distractor_rationales.D: This is the vibration percentage itself, not the increase relative to no notification.

passages.title: Working Memory, Sleep Restriction, and Retrieval Cues
passages.body:
A fictional laboratory study examined how one night of sleep restriction affects memory performance. Participants were randomly assigned to either a normal-sleep group or a restricted-sleep group. The next morning, all participants studied 30 neutral word pairs. After a 20-minute filler task, they completed two tests. In the free-recall test, participants wrote down as many target words as possible. In the cued-recall test, participants were shown the first word of each pair and attempted to retrieve the associated target word. Participants also completed a 2-back task as a measure of working memory updating.

Memory and working-memory performance
Group | Free recall: mean words recalled | Cued recall: mean words recalled | 2-back accuracy (%)
Normal sleep | 18.4 | 24.1 | 87
Restricted sleep | 13.2 | 20.2 | 73

Self-reported fatigue and motivation
Group | Fatigue rating, 1 to 7 | Motivation rating, 1 to 7
Normal sleep | 2.3 | 5.8
Restricted sleep | 5.9 | 5.6

Retrieval benefit — Both groups recalled more words on cued recall than on free recall, but the restricted-sleep group performed worse than the normal-sleep group on both tests.

questions.stem: Which interpretation is best supported by the difference between free recall and cued recall in both groups?

choices.text: Cued recall prevented encoding from occurring.
Retrieval cues improved access to encoded information.
Free recall measured only sensory memory.
The restricted-sleep group had no stored memories of the word pairs.

questions.explanation: Both groups recalled more words when given the first word of each pair. This pattern indicates that retrieval cues can improve access to information that was encoded and stored, even when free recall is lower. Common miss: Assuming lower free recall means information was never stored, rather than considering retrieval support. This is correct. Cues helped participants retrieve more target words. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractor_rationales.A: Cued recall occurs at test, after encoding; it does not prevent encoding.
distractor_rationales.C: Free recall of studied words after a filler task is not a measure of sensory memory.
distractor_rationales.D: The restricted-sleep group recalled many words, especially with cues, so stored memories were not absent.

questions.stem: The 2-back task used in the study most directly measures which cognitive process?

choices.text: Classical conditioning
Working memory updating
Absolute sensory threshold
